size.note: Length 26-29 cm, wingspan about 35-40 cm, 230-290 g; the largest North American quail. The build scales the standing model to 0.27 m bill to tail (tail fan included); the plumes stand 5.5 cm above the crown. One size for both sexes (instances scaled 0.9-1.1).

source.prompt: A mountain quail (Oreortyx pictus), a plump round ground bird like a small partridge, NOT a dove, NOT a songbird. One adult walking on the ground, side-on, body low and horizontal, a short thick neck, a very short rounded tail, short legs. Two long thin straight black plumes rising from the crown and leaning back over the nape. About 27 cm long. Slate blue-grey head, nape and breast; a chestnut throat outlined in white; chestnut flanks with bold white vertical bars; olive-brown back and wings; a short stout black bill. Realistic proportions. No base, no rock. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: The body re-skinned (a 56 x 30 UV sphere pushed out along rays from the body's centre to the outermost surface: the envelope over the generator's scale flaps, whose tunnels stopped Blender's collapse at ~550-1,100 faces) and the generator's own head and neck joined into it; the floating crest deleted and two procedural straight plumes added (5.5 cm, leaning 25 degrees back; asserted: tips above and behind their bases); the head carried lower and forward on a shorter neck; bill shortened 0.65x and widened 1.5x at the base; long legs cut at the belly and short grey procedural legs added; the thin blade tail deleted and a short rounded fan added; body tipped 6 degrees nose-down; scaled to 0.27 m; recoloured with faint per-face noise (+-4%) and a female colour set in _COLORB; flight wing cards added (8 % larger than the California quail's). Triangles: lod0 1,000 = 844 body + 156 (legs, wing cards, plumes, tail fan, eyes); lod1 400 = 326 + 74; lod2 119 = 94 + 25. Tiers switch at 12 and 40 m. GLB 270,308 bytes.

candidates.review: A slender dove or thrush, not a quail: a long upright neck, a long thin bill, a long tapered blade tail, long thin legs, no plumes. Clearly wrong for the body; the brief's prompt B (body low and horizontal, short neck, very short tail, partridge-like) was run instead and adopted.

candidates.purpose: the brief's prompt B (walking, body level); adopted
candidates.review: Reads as a plump partridge-shaped quail from the side: a round body carried level, a short neck, a small head, a short tail. Faults: the plume came out as a fan crest floating apart from the head over the back; the bill long and thin; the legs long and thin (one striding forward); the tail a thin blade; the breast and lower flanks sculpted as overlapping scale flaps (fins and tunnels). All fixed or replaced by the build.

accuracy_notes: Generated, not adopted from a download: no CC0 or CC BY mountain quail mesh exists. Reads as a mountain quail, not a California quail, at 3-15 m: two long straight black plumes standing up and back from the crown (not a forward teardrop), a slate blue-grey head, nape and breast, a chestnut throat bordered by a white line from the gape under the eye and down the side of the neck, chestnut flanks crossed by white bars, a cinnamon-buff belly, a dark chestnut undertail, an olive-brown back and wings, grey legs. Female variant (the nape and hindneck washed brown) for half the birds. Still open: the female's shorter plume is not drawn (one plume length for both, as the California quail's); the plumes do not lie back when it runs; the flank bars are as coarse as the triangles (four or five at lod0, a blotch at lod2); the buff line along the folded wing is faint; the head and the re-skinned body are two overlapping pieces (no seam is visible at the lineup's distances, but the far tier's neck is blocky); the body's width (11 cm) is at the plump end. A local birder should check the plume length and angle, the throat border and the posture.
